full.description: This image is a photomicrograph of urinary tract tissue, likely representing transitional epithelium (urothelium). The histological section displays stratified urothelial cells with characteristic morphology, showing a well-oriented arrangement and folded mucosal architecture. The left panel highlights the nuclear pattern, while the right panel shows the tissue architecture at slightly lower magnification. The appearance is consistent with normal transitional epithelium or a benign urothelial lesion.

blind.description: This is a micrograph of a skin biopsy showing irregular masses of basaloid cells infiltrating the dermis. The tumor cells exhibit a characteristic peripheral palisaded appearance and are separated from the surrounding stroma by a retraction artifact. These histological features are most consistent with basal cell carcinoma.

random.description: This image is a photomicrograph of urothelial tissue, possibly from the bladder or urinary tract. It displays transitional epithelium showing characteristic architecture, with highlighted cellular nuclei in the inset to emphasize the nuclear arrangement and stratification. The surrounding pink-stained stromal tissue provides structural support. Such histological sections are typically evaluated for urothelial hyperplasia, dysplasia, or transitional cell carcinoma.
